cohort: 100 pregnant women (50 with oligohydramnios and 50 with normal amniotic fluid index) receiving regular check-ups at hospitals affiliated with J.J.M. Medical College, Davangere.
finding: Oligohydramnios was associated with a higher incidence of thick meconium-stained liquor, fetal distress, operative delivery, caesarean section, lower Apgar scores, low birth weight, meconium aspiration, and increased perinatal morbidity and mortality.
